document.title: Phase 2: XPath 4.0 and F&O 4.0
document.p: Goal (PLAN.md): full XPath 4.0 syntax and the whole F&O 4.0 function library; the first public release. Gate: 90% of the applicable XP40 test cases pass (; Phase 1 ended at 21,443 of about 31,500, 68%). Packets are one agent session each and run in parallel in one working tree under the Phase 1 rules (, repeated below); the overlap with Phases 3 and 4 follows . Scope decisions (collations, HTML parsing, non-goals) are .

item.p: Ownership. Each packet names the files it owns; packets that run at the same time never share one. A file named by two packets belongs to the earlier wave; the later packet starts only after the earlier one is committed. Ledgers (docs/DECISIONS.md, GLOSSARY.md, LOG.md): one small insertion, committed at once and alone.

Registration is by glob. After , a library part is a file src/function_library_<part>.c defining sxml_function_library_<part>; the processor and the fuzz fixture find it without an edit. Evaluator parts and lowering parts (2.0, 2.1) work the same way.

Design packets may change headers; implementation packets must not (they write the need under "Proposed" in docs/DECISIONS.md). After the public headers change only through a decision record until the release (2.18) makes them stable ().

Every packet imitates its named golden files (default: src/memory.c, tests/memory_test.c; for a library part src/function_library_math.c and tests/function_library_test.c; for resumable natives src/function_library_higher_order.c); has allocation-failure loops and leak checks (sxml_item_heap_read_counts); cites the specification by section title; uses no C recursion (); is done when debug, debug-gcc and wasm pass, tools/lint.sh is clean, the slice holds at 198 and the XP40 pass count (docs/CONFORMANCE.md) has not dropped.

Acceptance names QT4 test sets. "fn-x ≥ N%" means the passed share of the applicable cases of that set in sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --test-set=fn-x, release build; the packet's LOG entry gives before and after counts.
The CLI is not a packet: it gains options (--decimal-format, text resources) only when a packet makes them real (docs/CLI.md).
